paper: Gottlieb & Shu (1998), Total variation diminishing Runge-Kutta schemes, Math. Comp. 67(221):73-85, DOI 10.1090/S0025-5718-98-00913-2
note: These are genuinely OPEN questions - not answered by our C1/C2/C3 tests, and not settled by the paper's own scope. They are grounded in the SSP/TVD Runge-Kutta framework for hyperbolic conservation laws.

questions.q: Is the empirical SSP coefficient c* = 1 that we recovered for SSP-RK2/3 (via binary search on step-IC + first-order upwind advection) robust across representative high-resolution spatial discretizations (limited MUSCL, WENO-5, WENO-Z) and problem classes (Burgers with sonic point, linear systems with characteristic decomposition), or does an adversarial IC / limiter combination expose a smaller usable CFL in practice?
questions.basis: Our C3 test fixed spatial op = 1st-order upwind, step IC, N=400, tolerance 1e-10. The critique section flags this explicitly: c*=1 was demonstrated for this configuration, not proven optimal across problem classes. The paper's SSP theory is proven relative to whichever spatial op is forward-Euler-TVD; whether c*=1 remains sharp for the ops practitioners actually deploy (WENO, limited MUSCL) at strong shocks is an empirical question.
next_steps: Rebuild the binary-search harness (work/ssp_rk_replication.py C3) parameterized on spatial op {upwind, minmod MUSCL, WENO-5, WENO-Z} and problem {linear advection step IC, Burgers Riemann, Sod shock tube}.
For each (scheme, spatial op, problem) triple, report empirical max CFL preserving TVD (or, for systems, a non-oscillation surrogate like maxwise TV of characteristic variables) to tolerance 1e-10.

Compare against the tighter Shu-Osher SSP bounds and against the Kubatko/Ketcheson/Ruuth SSP-RK survey coefficients for higher-stage schemes; document any gap between the theoretical c* and the empirical CFL a practitioner can actually use.

questions.q: For SSP-RK3 at CFL = 1.05 (0.05 past the SSP bound), we measured only a 5.5e-2 fractional TV increase, while SSP-RK2 at the same overshoot blew up by 3.3e+2. How sharply does each scheme transition from TVD to non-TVD as CFL increases, and does that transition curve match a predictable form (e.g. leading order in (CFL - c*))?
questions.basis: Our C2 tested exactly one point past the SSP boundary (CFL=1.05) and observed a 4-order-of-magnitude asymmetry in TV growth between RK2 and RK3. The paper predicts failure past c* but does not characterize how failure scales. The critique section flags this explicitly as a gap our tests do not close.
next_steps: Sweep CFL in {1.00, 1.01, 1.02, ..., 1.20} for SSP-RK2 and SSP-RK3 on the same step-IC + upwind + N=200 setup.
Plot fractional TV increase vs (CFL - c*) on log-log axes; fit a power law and report exponent and prefactor for each scheme.

Cross-check against the Shu-Osher formal analysis and, if the observed transition is sharper for RK2 than RK3, tie the exponent to the schemes' respective absolute-stability regions and monotonicity margins.

questions.q: Do the same optimal SSP coefficients and forward-Euler-preservation structure that Gottlieb & Shu (1998) prove for explicit RK carry over to implicit / diagonally-implicit / IMEX Runge-Kutta schemes needed for stiff spatial operators (parabolic terms, source terms, low-Mach acoustics), and if so which implicit families attain the sharpest SSP coefficients?
questions.basis: The 1998 paper is explicit-RK only. Real hyperbolic PDE codes routinely need implicit or IMEX time stepping when a stiff component is present. Whether the Shu-Osher convex-combination trick extends, and with what c*, is a genuinely open direction that the paper itself flags as future work in its concluding remarks (and that the SSP literature since 1998 - Ketcheson, Ruuth, Higueras - has partly, but not fully, resolved).
next_steps: Survey post-1998 implicit-SSP literature (Ketcheson 2008/2009 SIAM J. Numer. Anal.; Ketcheson-Macdonald-Gottlieb 2009 Appl. Numer. Math.; Higueras) and enumerate which implicit RK families have proven SSP coefficients and what those coefficients are.

Reproduce the c* for at least one canonical implicit SSP-RK (e.g. SDIRK SSP(3,3) or the Ketcheson optimal implicit SSP-RK2) on a stiff advection-diffusion test with method-of-lines + limited advection + implicit diffusion.
Report whether the implicit c* recovers, degrades, or exceeds the explicit c*=1 for equivalent stage counts, and whether IMEX splittings preserve the SSP property of their explicit component.

questions.q: Beyond the 3-stage explicit case, what is the sharp order-count-vs-SSP-coefficient tradeoff, in particular the paper's non-existence result for a 4-stage, order-4, all-positive-beta SSP-RK - does relaxing the all-positive constraint (allowing downwind operators, as in Shu-Osher) buy back an order-4 SSP scheme, and what is its optimal c*?
questions.basis: The paper explicitly proves non-existence of a 4-stage order-4 SSP-RK with all-positive beta and states the tradeoff must be broken by either extra stages, lower order, or admitting downwind operators. Our replication was minimum-scope and did not test the 4-stage case. This is an open direction the paper itself opens.
next_steps: Implement the paper's own eq. (4.3)-style 4-stage order-4 candidate with the paper's tabulated negative-beta pair, code a matching downwind operator L~(u) for a linear advection test, and measure the empirical SSP coefficient.
Compare against the Spiteri-Ruuth 2002 SIAM J. Numer. Anal. optimal explicit SSP-RK(s,p) tables (which explicitly quantify the extra-stages route) for s=5,...,10 at p=4.
Report, for each (s,p), the ratio c*/s (SSP efficiency) and identify the s at which SSP-RK4 becomes competitive with SSP-RK3 on wall-clock per accuracy for a canonical Euler shock tube.

questions.q: For a fully practical shock-capturing scheme (WENO-5 + SSP-RK3) on the 1D compressible Euler equations (Sod, Lax, Shu-Osher shock-density interaction), does the CFL bound predicted by SSP theory (CFL <= c* * Delta_t_FE with c* = 1) actually deliver a monotone / essentially-non-oscillatory solution at strong shocks, or is the effective CFL bound tighter in practice because the WENO spatial op is only conditionally forward-Euler-monotone?
questions.basis: SSP theory is proven relative to whichever spatial op is forward-Euler-TVD. WENO-5 is not exactly forward-Euler-TVD (it is essentially non-oscillatory, not total-variation-diminishing), so the c*=1 bound is a hypothesis-satisfies transferrence, not a proof. Whether SSP-RK3 + WENO-5 at CFL=1 delivers the ENO property at strong shocks is a load-bearing empirical question every production code implicitly answers. Our replication used only 1st-order upwind advection; we did not test this coupling.
next_steps: Implement WENO-5 (Jiang-Shu 1996 formulation) for 1D compressible Euler and drive it with SSP-RK3 (our eq. 4.2 implementation).
Run Sod, Lax, and Shu-Osher shock-density interaction at CFL in {0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.1}; report post-shock TV, L1 error against Riemann/reference, and visible oscillations.
Cross-reference against Shu 1998 lecture notes and Cockburn-Shu 1998 J. Sci. Comput. tables; document the effective practical CFL bound and whether it matches c*=1 or is tighter.
